newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat holds firm despite corn/soybean debacle.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat holds firm despite corn/soybean debacle.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures continued to hold firm near midsession despite a limit slide in nearby soybeans and sharply lower corn futures, traders said.
"Wheat is acting tremendous. They're buying wheat and selling corn and beans," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
USDA early Friday issued its October crop report which was bearish for corn and soybeans but bullish for wheat.

USDA cut its forecast for 1996-97 U.S. wheat ending stocks to 470 million bushels from the previous forecast for 506 million. The government also trimmed its outlook for world wheat ending stocks to 116.53 million tonnes, from the previous forecast for 117.43 million.
But some traders said the cut in stocks should not have been a big surprise.
"They cut the stocks but we expected that to happen. We got a hint of that happening in the stocks (Sep quarterly) report," Bruce said.
Wheat should begin a seasonal climb after the recent sharp drop in the market, they said.
At 1155 CDT, wheat was unchanged to one cent per bushel lower, with December down 1/4 at $4.23-3/4.
"There wasn't anything bearish for wheat this morning and wheat seasonally should be going up," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Volume was relatively thin with Cargill buying one-half million bushels of December and Prudential Securities buying one million Dec, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures sold one million bushels of December and ING Derivatives sold one half million bushels of December, they said.

Short term technical indicators also helped put a base under wheat with the 20-day moving average (MA) at Thursday's close at $4.25 for the December acting as a magnet. The four-day MA for Dec Thursday closed at $4.25-1/2, which also provided some upward pull for the nearby December contract.
At 1200 CDT, Dec's nine day relative strength index (RSI) was at 39.724 points. Technicians generally view an RSI of 30 or less as near oversold and 70 or higher as nearing overbought status.
